Try itKnow where the model stops: tires slide at high sideways acceleration

  • The model assumes each wheel rolls where it points.
  • A real tire slides sideways a little when the AV turns, and more the harder it turns.

  1. The model holds while the sideways acceleration \(v^2\kappa\) stays under half of what the tires can give:
    • on a dry road, \(\mu = 1\)
    • \(0.5\,\mu g = 0.5 \times 9.81 = 4.9\) m/s2
  2. Our curve: at most \(3.46^2 \times 0.1673 = 2.0\) m/s2, the profile's cap. Well inside.
  3. Harder turns need a model with tire slip: the dynamic bicycle model (in the docs).
arcspeed \(v\)try it
Speed alone does not set the limit: the sideways acceleration is \(v^2/R\), so a gentle curve allows more speed than a tight one.
